title: Stdio Compatibility Matrix Execution

diagnosis.mechanism: driver.run_session writes the full request batch (initialize/notifications-initialized/tools-list/tools-call) and closes stdin immediately; this races the real async MCP server's EOF-triggered shutdown against in-flight tools/call dispatch. Confirmed non-deterministic across 3 trials tapped (1/3 correlated) and reproduced identically without the tap (batched, no-tap: dropped too) -- tap is exonerated. A strictly sequential write-one/read-one exchange (manual-sequential-client) succeeds 1/1 through the tap.

Same batch-write/immediate-stdin-close race as mcp-server-time (see that entry); reproduced 3/3 tapped trials and in a direct no-tap batched run -- tap is exonerated. A sequential write-one/read-one exchange succeeds 1/1 through the tap; the isError result for the unroutable fetch still correlates and counts as success.

key_findings: Synthetic echo server: stable correlation across single and multi-call tests
MCP server time & fetch: reached server but correlation incomplete (real server behavior)
MCP Python SDK: successfully initialized via stdio tap wrapper
Abrupt shutdown (SIGKILL): partial requests logged, JSONL remained parseable
